content.comment_body: Hello, I'm looking to create a button in the [product_name] web editor that triggers an output based on how long the button is pressed. This is for some dimmers that activate with a short pulse and adjust with a longer pulse. I know how to make a button in the web editor, but currently it only works in a bistable mode. Could anyone assist? Grtz

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. What you're trying to achieve isn't possible with the extended web server. The extended web server only handles static signals and can't pass the signal for the duration that the button is pressed.

Hi, thanks for the welcome. I understand this is the place for expert advice, so I appreciate your response. Isn't it unfortunate that this feature isn't available even in 2020? I purchased a [company_name] controller, power supply, and extra I/O modules, but now can't use them as intended. I've checked online and most modular dimmers use push-button functionality. As someone not deeply experienced, does this mean I have to buy new, costly dimmers and use analog output for dimming, or is there another simple solution? Thanks for your help. Grtz [user_name]

As previously mentioned, the extended web server can't evaluate how long the mouse button is pressed, so it won't set a bit HIGH for that duration. It only reacts to the edge change when the button is clicked, setting a bit HIGH which remains HIGH until clicked again. You can control this bit inside the [product_name] program and set it to LOW within the program, creating an impulse for a single cycle. This can be used to manage a delay for switching off, delivering a timed pulse.

Thank you for the explanation. It seems it's not possible to create a pulse matching the duration of a touchscreen click, so dimming isn't feasible as it requires direct user interaction. I'm disappointed. Sorry [company_name], I had to choose a different home automation system.

Another idea: Consider using the basic web server together with the TDE display. The TDE doesn't need to be physically present. In this setup, the F key in the [product_name] program stays HIGH as long as it is pressed via the web server. Refer to the attached video for more details.

Thanks, but I need a solution where anyone can access the buttons through a well-designed web interface. I ordered a pulse dimmer that integrates with Google Home; this might be the most cost-effective option. Grtz

analysis.insight_summary: Users are frustrated by the limitations of the [product_name] web editor and extended web server, particularly their inability to produce monostable outputs where the output pulse matches the button press duration. The current system only allows for bistable operation, which is unsuitable for common modular dimmer setups requiring press-duration control. This gap makes the products incompatible with user needs for intuitive dimmer adjustment.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] web editor to allow monostable button control, sending output pulses that match the length of button presses, for intuitive and effective dimming functionality through the web interface.
